notes: A054656_formula: for n >= 23, a n = 2 if n-6, n-4 prime, 1 if one of n-6, n-4, n-1 prime, 0 otherwise, where a n counts primes p <= n in no finite set of primes summing to n. Route: two primes in (x,2x] for x >= 6 (Erdos-Bertrand with one extra factor 2x for x >= 512, prime chain below); Richert-type induction: every m > 27 is a sum of distinct primes avoiding any given p; table for m <= 27 (exceptions (m,p) all with m+p <= 22); p missing iff n-p in {1,4,6}. a(22) = 1 shows n >= 23 is sharp. Axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. Outside Lean: none (agreement of a with the OEIS data terms checked by certificate/check.py, n <= 3000).

sources.cite: H.-E. Richert, Uber Zerfallungen in ungleiche Primzahlen, Math. Z. 52 (1949) 342-343
sources.what: every integer > 6 is a sum of distinct primes (the method used here)

prior_art.note: No proof of the conjecture found; the avoid-one-prime Richert induction and the two-primes Bertrand step are ours (both standard in spirit).
